title: Connectome distance to motor output predicts movement encoding in mouse and fly brain regions, but not beyond geometry in larval zebrafish; in mouse the link is not specific to movement
abstract: Question: a campaign result in C. elegans found that neuron classes with a shorter connectome random walk to muscle encode locomotion more strongly. Does this motor-proximity rule apply to region-level connectomes of other animals? Method: one measure for all species, the log expected hitting time of a random walk on the directed region connectome to a motor-output set, related to public movement-encoding scores. Mouse: Knox 2019 connectome, brainstem motor and spinal-projecting nuclei, IBL Brain-Wide Map wheel-speed encoding (170 regions). Fly: FlyWire v783 synapse walk to descending and motor neurons, Aimon 2023 walk R2 (75 regions, 16 flies). Larval zebrafish: mapZebrain projectome, reticulospinal regions, cross-validated spontaneous swim R2 from Legare 2025 two-photon data (59 regions, 14 fish). Pre-registered nulls: geometry-preserving rewiring, and rewiring with output weights kept. Results: mouse rho = -0.52, outside all 1,000 nulls of both kinds, partial rho -0.45 after distance and strength. But the same hitting time predicted stimulus, choice and feedback encoding equally (speed minus stimulus contrast -0.01, CI -0.14 to 0.14), and random caudal target sets gave rho -0.40. Fly rho = -0.80, but rewiring among neuropils with descending-neuron input kept gave the same value (-0.83), and distance to descending-neuron input sites alone gave -0.84. Zebrafish rho = -0.32 (negative in 14 of 14 fish), but geometry-preserving rewiring gave the same value (p = 0.48) and the partial rho after distance to the reticulospinal regions was -0.07. Conclusion: the rank relation is present in four animals, but wiring beyond geometry explains it only in worm and mouse, and in mouse it is a general task-encoding gradient, not a movement-specific one. Limitations: cross-region correlations, different encoding scores per species, coarse fly imaging, few fish swim bouts, a judgement-based mouse motor set.
